title: jk.toml
description: JumpKick project manifest. Top-level identity and language keys, the core tables, and the dependency scopes. Plugin-owned tables ([micronaut], [android], ...) are allowed and documented by their plugins.

name.description: Module identity; never inherited from the workspace.

group.description: Maven groupId, or { workspace = true } in a member.

version.description: Version string, or { workspace = true } in a member.

jdk.description: The project's JDK vendor and version, the one spelling: jdk = { vendor = "corretto", version = "21", required = true }. Each key is optional; version is a major ("21"), an exact build ("25.0.4.1") or a floor within one major (">=25.0.5"); required (default false) binds which JDK builds the project and which cached results serve it, where by default it is a suggestion. A workspace root's jdk applies to members; { workspace = true } inherits it explicitly. The string forms ("temurin-25", "=temurin-25.0.4") are retired.

cache.description: How this project takes cached compile and test results made on other JDKs.

jdk-match.description: Which JDKs' cached results serve a compile or a suite: "major" (default) any vendor and patch of the major this build uses, "level" any JDK at or above the module's java level, "build" only the same vendor, version and build. JK_CACHE_JDK_MATCH overrides it for one shell; ~/.jk/config.toml's [cache] jdk-match is the user's default.

sources.description: Sources jar: true → assembled by jk publish only; "always" → built by jk package. A library (no [application]) builds it regardless.

javadoc.description: Javadoc jar for a library. Unset (default): written by jk publish and jk javadoc, not by jk build; true: every build, lenient (-Xdoclint:none, warnings in the results); "strict": every build, javadoc's doclint checks fail the step; false: never.

repositories.description: [repositories] table: one entry per remote, keyed by the name jk-lock.toml records as the source. An entry is a URL string or a table.

url.description: Base URL: https://, s3://, gs://, or file://. Plaintext http:// needs allow-insecure.

publish-url.description: Where jk publish writes and reads back, when not url (a bucket behind a CDN, a hosted repository behind a group). Same schemes as url. Resolvers and the lock never use it. Refused on central, google and jumpkick.

token.description: Bearer token; ${VAR} expands when the repository is used.

username.description: Basic-auth user; ${VAR} expands when the repository is used.

password.description: Basic-auth password; ${VAR} expands when the repository is used.

access-key.description: Object-store access key; ${VAR} expands when the repository is used.

secret-key.description: Object-store secret key; ${VAR} expands when the repository is used.

session-token.description: Object-store session token; ${VAR} expands when the repository is used.

groups.description: Exclusive Maven groups: exact or prefix.* patterns that resolve only from this repository.

allow-insecure.description: Accept a plaintext http:// URL for this repository. Refused on central.

blocked.description: The repository is asked of nothing and named when a package resolves nowhere, as Maven 3.9 blocks a plaintext http repository; written by jk import for a POM-declared http URL. Not beside allow-insecure.

optional.description: A repository the lock can do without: once nothing answers at its address it is passed over like a blocked one, and named when a package resolves nowhere, instead of stopping the resolve. Written by jk import for every POM-declared repository; implied for a loopback URL.

allow-unverified.description: Pin an artifact this repository publishes no .sha256/.sha1 sidecar for; the lock summary counts them. Refused on central.

releases.description: Ask this repository for release versions (default true). false makes it snapshot-only.

snapshots.description: Ask this repository for -SNAPSHOT versions (default true). false makes it releases-only.

profiles.description: [profiles] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

features.description: [features] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

workspace.description: [workspace] (workspace root): the member modules and the dependency versions they share. See docs/user/workspaces.md.

modules.description: Member module directories, relative to the root; a glob such as "libs/*" names every match.

dependencies.description: One shared dependency per key: a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact:version string, or { group, name, version } or { git, group, ... }. A member pins it with { workspace = true }.

manifest.description: [manifest] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

plugins.description: [plugins] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

minified.description: Package a minified (R8) jar; implies assembly. R8 settings live in [minified].

native.description: Build a GraalVM native image of the application. Image settings live in [native].

config.description: Module-relative template jk install renders into ~/.jk/config/<bin>/config.toml.

relocate.description: Package relocation in the fat jar: source package prefix to shaded package prefix.

jvm-args.description: Flags jk run and jk dev put on the application JVM, such as --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED.

lib-dir.description: Write target/<name>.jar with a Class-Path manifest and its runtime jars under target/<dir>/ (true means libs).

lib-versions.description: Whether the lib-dir jar file names carry their versions (default true).

lib-exclude.description: Runtime dependencies left out of the lib-dir layout: artifact, group:artifact or group:*.

native.description: [native]: build a GraalVM native image of the module with jk native, and with jk build when enabled = "always" (docs/user/native.md). The table alone enables it.

enabled.description: true (default): jk native builds the image; "always": jk build does too; false: the table stays but no image is built.

main.description: The main class of the image. Default the module's main.

name.description: The image's file name. Default the module name; a trailing .exe is ignored.

graal.description: The GraalVM that builds the image: "graalvm-25", "25" or "native". Default a GraalVM of the project's own major.

graal-vendor.description: The GraalVM distribution's vendor, beside graal-version.

graal-version.description: The GraalVM version, 25 or "25.0.4", beside graal-vendor.

metadata-repository.description: The GraalVM reachability-metadata repository release, in the dependency version grammar: "latest" (default), "^1" or an exact "1.1.4".

image.description: [image] table: what jk image builds and where jk publish pushes it. A member's table sits over the workspace root's, which sits over ~/.jk/config.toml's. Keys are documented in docs/user/images.md.

base.description: Base image reference; {java-major-version} is the module's java. Default: a slim JRE of the module's java.

name.description: Image repository. Default the module's artifact id. Never inherited from the workspace root.

user.description: The user the container runs as.

ports.description: Ports the image exposes. Never inherited from the workspace root.

env.description: Environment of the image, and of its AOT training runs. JAVA_OPTS is the JVM-flag hook: its tokens lead the entrypoint.

training-env.description: Environment of the AOT training runs alone, laid over env; never in the image.

registry.description: Registry jk publish pushes the image to ("ghcr.io/acme"); jk image names the image it loads after it. Default: none, no image lane.

tag.description: Image tag. Default the module version.

main.description: Main class the entrypoint runs. Default the module's main. Never inherited from the workspace root.

docker-executable.description: The docker-compatible CLI (docker, podman, nerdctl) for Dockerfile mode and container training.

docker-file.description: Module-relative Dockerfile; builds with docker build instead of the daemonless builder. Never inherited from the workspace root.

aot-cache.description: Train a JVM AOT cache into the image. Refused on a node module.

kind.description: "static" serves a node build's output from nginx. Omit for the module's own image.

referrers.description: Attach the SBOM and SLSA provenance to a registry push as OCI referrers. Default true.

sigstore.description: Sign a registry push's SLSA provenance with Sigstore keyless and attach it in a DSSE envelope, on every jk publish push. Default false.

train.description: [train] table: what jk train runs to record the application's reflection, resource and proxy use. Keys are documented in docs/user/dynamic-surface.md.

command.description: Command that exercises the application under the tracing agent. Default: the tests tagged train.

commit-to.description: Module-relative directory the merged training output is copied to, for committing. Must stay under the module.

require-fresh.description: Fail a build whose training output is missing or out of date instead of using it. Default false.

aot-cache.description: Also write a JVM AOT cache from the training run. Default false.

profile.description: [[train.profile]]: training runs whose results are unioned. Default: one profile named default.

name.description: The profile's name; jk train --profile selects it.

properties.description: System properties of this profile's run.

args.description: Program arguments of this profile's run.

build.description: [build] table: how this module compiles and tests. Keys are documented in docs/user/build.md.

order-after.description: Modules this one builds after, without a classpath edge.

test-plugin-jars.description: Plugin jars handed to the test JVM, each built before this module's tests. A short name is the first-party worker jk-<name> when the workspace has one (helidon is jk-helidon, not a rule pack named helidon); a group:name coordinate is exactly that module.

debug.description: Debug information javac writes: full (-g: source, lines, local variables; the default, as Gradle and Maven compile), lines (-g:source,lines) or none (-g:none). A compile input.

ksp-options.description: KSP processor options as key=value strings.

ksp-version.description: The KSP2 release this module's KSP round runs, an exact version. Absent: jk's own pin, which moves with jk releases. jk update moves this pin like any tool pin.

extra-src.description: Extra module-relative source roots compiled with the main sources.

generated-src.description: Committed generated source roots: compiled with the main sources, never formatted.

cache-heavy-outputs.description: false keeps this module's heavy outputs (native images, fat jars, jlink images: 32 MiB or more) out of the cache, so they live only where they were built. The window they stay cached for is the machine's [cache] heavy-ttl; a project can only turn caching off (default true).

module-services.description: Write META-INF/services/<service> into the classes tree for every provides in the compiled module-info, so ServiceLoader on a class path or processor path finds the providers (default false).

test.description: [test] table: how this module's tests compile and run. Keys are documented in docs/user/test.md.

workers.description: Test JVMs for this module: 0 = the build's auto share, 1 = serial.

extra-src.description: Extra module-relative test source roots or single files, compiled into whichever suites are selected. Helpers a sibling consumes belong in fixtures.

fixtures.description: A source root compiled to target/test-fixtures/classes, on every suite's classpath and never an artifact. true is src/fixtures/java; a string names the module-relative root.

serial-tags.description: Class-level JUnit tags whose classes run on one trailing worker instead of sharing the sharded pool. A no-op when workers is 1.

coverage.description: Every test JVM of this module runs under the JaCoCo agent and the module leaves its coverage report, as jk test -T does. Default false.

tools.description: External executables the tests run, by the bare name they invoke (a path is refused). Where each resolves on PATH and its --version are run-tests inputs.

env.description: Environment of each forked test JVM: a bare name forwards the caller's value when set; a table sets values (${VAR}, ${module} and ${target} expand). Laid over [env] for test JVMs. A run-tests input.

guard-suites.description: The suites jk test -g runs, read from the workspace root. Default ["test", "integration"].

assertions.description: Run every forked test JVM with -ea, as Surefire and Gradle do. Default true; false runs the suite with Java and Kotlin assert statements disabled. A run-tests input: flipping it re-runs the suite.

failure-snapshot.description: A failed test's agent report carries the arguments and locals at the frame that threw and the project frames above it, read through a debugger each test JVM attaches to itself. Default false. Not under --debug-jvm, nor when [test] jvm-args load a JDWP agent.

fast-method-budget.description: A fast-tier (untagged) test method that takes longer than this is a warning naming the method and its time; the run still passes. A duration ("1s", "500ms", "2m") or seconds. Set at the workspace root it holds every member; a member's own value wins. Absent: no budget.

cache.description: How a suite that did not pass whole is rerun under an unchanged stamp. "class" (the default) runs only the classes that have not passed; "module" runs the whole suite again, for suites whose classes share state and break when some are left out.

idle-timeout.description: How long a test JVM may print nothing (no test started, none finished) before it is taken for hung and stopped, its class reported as the failure. A duration ("90s", "45m", "120m") or seconds; holds the one suite JVM and every pool runner. Absent: 30 minutes for the suite JVM, 10 minutes stretched by host load for a pool runner.

locale.description: The test JVM's default locale, a BCP 47 tag ("de-DE"), forked as -Duser.language/-Duser.country, with LC_ALL and LANG a fixed UTF-8 locale (C.UTF-8; en_US.UTF-8 on macOS). Default "en-US", so the shell's LANG and LC_* neither reach a suite nor key it. "inherit" hands the test JVM the locale of the shell that ran jk and keys the suite on it.

timezone.description: The test JVM's default time zone, a zone id ("Europe/Berlin"), forked as -Duser.timezone with TZ set to it. Default "UTC", so neither the shell's TZ nor the engine's zone reaches a suite or keys it. "inherit" hands the test JVM the TZ of the shell that ran jk (else the machine's zone) and keys the suite on it.

network.description: A suite that reaches past this host runs on every build unless this says "allowed": its author vouching that what it reaches does not change its outcome, so its green marker is kept.

quarantine.description: When jk quarantines a test class on its own: one that fails and then passes on a re-run with nothing changed `flakes` times in its last `runs` runs (default { flakes = 2, runs = 20 }) is added to .jk/test/quarantine.toml, where a failure no longer fails the run. false: never. Read from the workspace root.

failures.description: Whether a failing test fails the run. "report" keeps every failure in jk-results.md and the JUnit XML and lets the run succeed (Maven's maven.test.failure.ignore); a compile error, a crashed test JVM or a timeout still fails. Default "fail". --test-failures and JK_TEST_FAILURES override it.

exclude-classes.description: Class patterns in --class syntax (fully qualified, simple name in any package, * wildcards) no suite runs, nested classes included; Surefire's <excludes>. A run-tests input.

exclude-dependencies.description: group:artifact coordinates left off every test JVM's classpath, declared or transitive; compile-test still sees them and the lock is unchanged. Surefire's <classpathDependencyExcludes>. A run-tests input.

exclude-src.description: Globs over a test source's path under its source root (**/ also matches at the root); matching files are not compiled by compile-test. The compiler plugin's <testExcludes>.

jvm-args.description: Flags appended verbatim to every forked test JVM after jk's own tuning (-Xmx, -Xss, --add-opens, an agent); Surefire's <argLine>. A run-tests input.

system-properties.description: One -Dkey=value per entry on every forked test JVM, a number or boolean rendered as its string; Surefire's <systemPropertyVariables>. A run-tests input.

suites.description: [test.suites.<name>]: suites that claim tests by class pattern over the default suite's sources, by JUnit tag from every test source, or both. The default suite leaves every claimed test out; jk test --suite <name> (or --guard for integration) runs them from the same compile.

classes.description: Class patterns in --class syntax (fully qualified, simple name in any package, * wildcards), nested classes included; Failsafe's <includes>, e.g. ["IT*", "*IT", "*ITCase"]. A run-tests input.

tags.description: JUnit tag names: every test carrying one belongs to the suite, from whichever test source it comes, and no suite directory runs it. A tag on a class covers its tests. A run-tests input.

exclude-classes.description: Class patterns among the suite's classes that run in no suite: the suite skips them and the default suite does not take them back; Failsafe's <excludes>. A run-tests input.

exclude-tags.description: JUnit tag names among the suite's tests that run in no suite: the suite skips them and the default suite does not take them back. A run-tests input.

env.description: Environment for the suite's own test JVMs, on top of [test] env; the suite wins a name both set. A run-tests input of the runs that select the suite.

jvm-args.description: Flags for the suite's own test JVMs, after [test] jvm-args. A run-tests input of the runs that select the suite.

system-properties.description: One -Dkey=value each on the suite's own test JVMs. A run-tests input of the runs that select the suite.

timeout.description: Per-method limit ("90s", "5m", "500ms" or seconds): a method past it fails after a thread dump, run on a separate thread so one that ignores interrupts still fails.

explicit.description: Run only when named (-s, guard-suites), never under --all.

dev.description: [dev] table: what `jk dev` runs beside the application, and how it tells the application itself is listening. Read by no other verb; never part of an action key.

sidecars.description: One table per sidecar, keyed by name, started in this order.

command.description: A string split like a shell would (quotes group; a backslash is literal unless it precedes a quote, a space, or a backslash; no expansion, no shell) or an argv array.

cwd.description: Working directory, relative to the manifest that declares the sidecar. Default "." (the manifest's own directory).

env.description: Values laid over the inherited environment and the .env files. Default: none.

ready.description: HTTP(S) URL polled every 250 ms (HTTP/1.1) until it answers 2xx/3xx; `localhost` is tried on both loopbacks. Default: no URL probe — with neither `ready` nor `ready-pattern`, one second alive is ready.

ready-pattern.description: Regex matched against the sidecar's stdout and stderr lines; the alternative to `ready`. Default: none.

ready-timeout.description: How long a probe may take: "60s", "2m", "500ms", or a bare number of seconds. A probe that times out fails the `jk dev` session. Default "60s".

front-door.description: Print this sidecar's `ready` URL in the one `ready ·` line once the whole session is ready. Default false.

run-before.description: Start the app only once this sidecar's probe has passed, for a database or broker the app needs at startup. Sidecars without it start alongside the app. Default false.

restart.description: What to do when the sidecar exits on its own: `never` reports the exit once and the session continues; `on-exit` restarts with backoff, up to five failures in a row. Default "never".

ready.description: The application's own probe: an HTTP(S) URL polled every 250 ms (HTTP/1.1) after each start and restart until it answers 2xx/3xx; `localhost` is tried on both loopbacks. `dev-ready` and the `ready ·` line wait for it. Default: no probe — the app counts as ready once forked.

ready-pattern.description: Regex matched against the application's stdout and stderr lines; the alternative to `ready`. On a terminal this pipes the app's output through jk so it can be read. Default: none.

ready-timeout.description: How long the application's probe may take: "60s", "2m", "500ms", or a bare number of seconds. A probe that times out fails the `jk dev` session, as a sidecar's does. Default "60s".

run.description: [run] table: what jk knows about the running application beyond its command (docs/user/mcp.md#run).

log.description: A file the application writes its log to, relative to the module. The MCP run tool's logs action tails it after the app's stdout and stderr.

format.description: [format]: how jk format and jk guard shape Java and Kotlin sources (docs/user/format.md).

style.description: A cross-language preset: "standard" is palantir for Java and kotlinlang for Kotlin.

java.description: The Java style, over style. Default "palantir".

kotlin.description: The Kotlin style, over style. Default "kotlinlang".

optimize-imports.description: Shorten fully qualified names and add imports (Java). Default true.

enforce.description: jk guard formats the sources that changed before it builds; under CI it checks instead. Default false.

ratchet-from.description: With enforce, only files changed since this git ref's merge-base, such as "origin/main".

exclude.description: Globs, relative to the workspace root, of files never formatted, such as "vendor/**".

resolve.description: [resolve] table: how platform BOMs and unmanaged diamonds resolve, and whether repositories a dependency's POM declares are consulted. Your own exact pins and every transitive resolve highest-wins; there is no pin policy.

platform.description: enforced (default): a BOM's version is the version. floor: a BOM's version is a lower bound highest-wins may raise.

unmapped.description: mediate (default): a module no BOM manages resolves to the highest version its POMs declare. strict: an unmanaged diamond is an error.

pom-repositories.description: use (default): a repository a dependency's POM declares is consulted for that POM's subtree, after [repositories]. ignore: only the repositories the project declares are consulted.

variants.description: [variants] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

jvm.description: [jvm] table: the flags of the worker JVMs JumpKick forks (compilers, plugin workers, the formatter). --ram-percent, --jvm-arg and the JK_JVM_* variables win over it. See docs/user/engine.md#worker-jvm-flags.

max-ram-percent.description: Per-JVM heap cap as a percentage of RAM, shared among the JVMs a step starts together; --ram-percent's table spelling.

gc.description: The workers' collector, in any case: g1, zgc, parallel or serial; default or none leaves it to the JVM.

string-dedup.description: String deduplication under g1 or zgc. Default true.

args.description: Extra flags for every worker JVM, before --jvm-arg and JK_JVM_ARGS.

deny.description: [deny] table: the policy jk deny checks the lock against. Keys are documented in docs/user/publish.md.
Repository hosts no locked artifact may come from; a host matches exactly or as a DNS-label suffix.
SPDX id globs; a row whose every licence matches is refused.

allow.description: SPDX id globs; a row needs one licence that matches.

yanked.description: The yanked policy. Only "allow" is accepted until enforcement ships.

env.description: [env] table: what this module's workers (the compiler, each test JVM, plugin steps) take from the environment beyond jk's allow-list. A test JVM also reads any other variable of the shell running jk when it looks it up, and the suite is keyed on what it read. Per module; inherit = false and scope set at a workspace root apply to every member. The declared names' values key the module's suite.

require.description: Variables taken from the shell running jk (or .env) that the module cannot do without. A goal that runs the module's tests or launches it fails the module before it compiles when one is unset, naming the variable and this line. Their values key the suite by digest; a name that looks like a credential is masked in output too.

optional.description: Variables taken from the shell running jk (or .env) when set; absent, never empty, when not. Their values key the suite like require's.

vars.description: Literal values, as tables: { TZ = "UTC" } (${VAR}, ${module} and ${target} expand; an unset ${VAR} is an error). A bare name is refused: declare it in optional or require. Reaches every worker of the module; [test] env layers on top for test JVMs.

inherit.description: true hands every worker of the module, the compiler included, the whole environment of the shell running jk, secrets included, and keys its suite on all of it less what a shell changes per command; costs cache hits, so write the reason beside it. false, written, is strict: test JVMs get the allow-list and the declared names alone, as before 0.53, and a run names each variable a test looked up that the shell sets; at a workspace root it holds for every member. Unwritten (the default), a test JVM reads any variable of the shell running jk when it looks it up, and the suite is keyed on what it read.

scope.description: Name patterns (a name, or a prefix ending in *: "SPRING_*") that narrow what a test JVM sees of the caller's undeclared variables: only matching names, besides the allow-list and the declared names. A suite that lists the environment's names then keys on the matching names alone, so its result holds on another host. A member's own scope wins over the workspace root's.

audit.description: [audit] table: what `jk audit` reports without gating on. Read by the audit alone; never part of an action key.

ignore.description: Advisories the audit reports as ignored and leaves out of the exit status, in this order (the first entry naming an advisory wins).

id.description: The advisory id as the audit reports it (GHSA-…, CVE-…).

reason.description: Why the finding is accepted. Required; an entry without one is refused.

until.description: Last day the entry ignores (ISO YYYY-MM-DD). From the day after, the finding gates again and is reported as `ignore expired`.

guards.description: [guards] table: on-build (default true) moves the module and workspace guard lanes to --guard when false; coverage-report names the coverage XML the coverage.* measures read. Rules live in jk-guards.toml.

graph.description: [graph] table (workspace root): [graph.aliases] maps a term in the code to the outside words that should find it. See docs/user/graph.md.

anchor-tail.description: What a passing build's MCP build verdict says of the places a hand edit left under an old name. silent (default): the places that must change, in five files at most; off: nothing, and the verdict waits for nothing; count, kinds (experimental): those and a count of the prose. See docs/user/graph.md.

config.description: [config]: CLI preferences of the project, under the flags and the environment and over ~/.jk/config.toml (docs/user/config.md).

force-ansi.description: Emit ANSI even into a file, or under TERM=dumb or CI.

notify.description: Desktop notification when a run takes a minute or more. Default "auto".

build-output.description: Show the live plan's process-output peek (Ctrl-O).

forge.description: [forge] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

kotlin-plugins.description: [[kotlin-plugins]]: Kotlin compiler plugins loaded into the module's Kotlin compiles, one table per plugin. A compile input.

coordinate.description: The plugin jar, group:artifact[:version]; without a version, the module's Kotlin compiler version. Name the -embeddable artifact.

id.description: The plugin's registered id, the <id> in kotlinc's -P plugin:<id>:<key>=<value>; set it whenever options is set. Defaults to the artifact name.

options.description: The plugin's options, each "key=value", as kotlinc's -P plugin:<id>:key=value takes them.

javac.description: [javac] table: the javac plugins compile-main and compile-test invoke, and verbatim javac args. A compile input — part of the compile action key.

plugins.description: One table per plugin, keyed by the plugin's registered javac name (case-sensitive; passed as -Xplugin:<name>). The jar is a [processor-dependencies] entry.

options.description: Options handed to the plugin after its name.

args.description: Verbatim javac arguments, appended after every plugin.

test.description: [javac.test]: the same two keys, plus `release`; when present this table replaces [javac] for compile-test (an empty table turns the plugins off for the suite).

release.description: The `--release` compile-test targets, when the suite is to use a newer API than the module's `java` level: a java = 17 library tested with JDK 21 test code. Not below `java`; compile-main and the published class-file level are untouched. Default: the module's `java`.

nullness.description: [nullness]: null checking by NullAway over JSpecify annotations (docs/user/build.md). The table brings JSpecify, Error Prone and NullAway and folds the flags they need into [javac]; a jar the module declares itself keeps its version. A compile input.

include.description: The packages checked, sub-packages included. Default: the module's group. [] checks only code under @NullMarked. @NullMarked and @NullUnmarked in package-info.java or on a class still apply.

exclude.description: Packages left unchecked, sub-packages included, even inside include. Default [].

explicit.description: Every top-level class must sit under @NullMarked or @NullUnmarked, at the table's severity. Default false.

severity.description: What a finding is: "error" (default) fails the compile; "warn" reports it.

options.description: Further Error Prone flags, after the table's own: -XepOpt:NullAway:KnownInitializers=…, -XepOpt:NullAway:ExcludedClassAnnotations=…

tests.description: Check compile-test too. Default false: a suite hands null to code on purpose.

m2.description: [m2] table; keys are documented in docs/user.

install.description: [install]: where jk install puts the jar and POM (docs/user/packaging.md). product-lib and product-bin are jk installing itself.

destination.description: jk (default) is jk's private repos/jk-local; m2 is the Maven local repository, ~/.m2/repository, and the default on a machine whose [m2] integration is "share". A workspace member inherits the root's.

dokka.description: [dokka]: how a Kotlin or mixed module's javadoc jar is documented (docs/user/packaging.md). A pure Java module never reads it.

version.description: The Dokka release: a bare version pins, ^2 floats within the line, latest is the newest stable. Default "2.2.0".

format.description: What Dokka writes into the jar: "javadoc" (default), the javadoc-shaped output Central's javadoc jar convention expects, or Dokka's own "html".

resources.description: [resources]: resource roots beyond the layout's, and roots whose files are expanded while copied (Maven's resource filtering) (docs/user/layout.md).

dirs.description: Extra main resource roots, module-relative, copied as written.

filtered.description: Main resource roots whose files are expanded: a placeholder of the delimiters (${name} and @name@ by default) becomes the value of name; a backslash keeps one literal; an unresolved ${name} is left as written and warned. Images and non-UTF-8 files are copied as they are. A layout root may be listed.

test-filtered.description: Test resource roots whose files are expanded.

delimiters.description: The placeholders filtering expands, as Maven's resources plugin spells them: <begin>*<end> (${*}, #{*}) or one token for both ends (@). ["@"] leaves ${name} for the application to resolve at run time.

properties.description: Values the expansion uses, over project.groupId, project.artifactId and project.version, which jk sets itself. Quote dotted names: "remoting.version" = "…".

jlink.description: [jlink]: package a custom runtime image target/<name>-jri/ of an application: a runtime linked from the project JDK with the modules jdeps finds, the jar and its runtime jars under app/, bin/start, and a startup cache trained by starting the image (docs/user/packaging.md). The table alone is the whole declaration.

modules.description: JDK modules linked beside the ones jdeps finds, such as "jdk.crypto.ec".

strip-debug.description: Drop debug attributes from the linked runtime. Default true.

aot-cache.description: The startup cache: true (default) is an AOT cache on JDK 25+ and a CDS archive below, "cds" a CDS archive on any JDK, false none.

jvm-args.description: JVM flags bin/start runs with; the training runs use them too.

args.description: Application arguments bin/start passes when it is given none.

start-timeout.description: Seconds a training or test start may run before it is asked to stop. Default 60.

test-start.description: Start the image once at build time to prove it runs. Default true; false needs aot-cache = false.

training-env.description: Environment variables the build's starts see and the image does not.

war.description: [war]: package a web archive beside the jar, exploded to target/<name>/ and archived to target/<name>.war (docs/user/packaging.md). The table alone is the whole declaration.

name.description: The file name without .war (Maven's finalName). Default <name>-<version>.

webapp.description: Module-relative directory copied to the war's root. Default "src/main/webapp".

multi-release.description: [multi-release]: each key a Java release (9 or newer), each value the source root or roots compiled at that release into the jar's META-INF/versions/<release>/ (docs/user/packaging.md). The jar gets Multi-Release: true.

build-info.description: [build-info]: the jar carries git.properties (git.commit.id, git.commit.id.abbrev, git.branch, git.commit.time, git.dirty, git.build.time, git.build.version, git.closest.tag.name) and, for a Spring Boot application, META-INF/build-info.properties. An empty table is the battery at its defaults (docs/user/packaging.md).

file.description: Resource path of the git properties file inside the jar. Default "git.properties".

time.description: What git.build.time and build.time record: "commit" (default) is the HEAD commit's time, so one commit's builds are byte-identical; "build" is the wall clock, so every build regenerates the file and repackages the jar.

publish.description: [publish]: the POM metadata a release carries (docs/user/publish.md). A workspace root's table applies to every member that declares none. Maven Central requires all of them.

repository.description: Where `jk publish` sends a release: a [repositories.<name>] entry, or "central". `jk publish --repository` overrides it for one run.

release.description: Where `jk publish` sends the deliverables (fat jars, archives, runtime images, native executables): github (a GitHub Release of the repository the git remote origin names) or an s3:// or gs:// prefix. The workspace root's value governs the workspace. See docs/user/publish.md#releasing-deliverables.

sign.description: Sign the release. Default true: a key-file means PGP, and CI that offers an identity token adds keyless Sigstore. false publishes unsigned (Central refuses that).

key-file.description: The PGP signing key file, relative to the module or ~/-prefixed. Central requires one. The passphrase never goes here (JK_GPG_PASSPHRASE).

sbom.description: Upload the CycloneDX and SPDX SBOMs beside the artifact. Default true.

provenance.description: Upload the SLSA provenance statement beside the artifact. Default true.

hold.description: Stop a Central upload at VALIDATED and leave the release to the Portal. Default false: jk publishes the deployment itself.

skip.description: When true, jk publish and jk install leave this module out (a test harness, an example, a site tool); it still builds and tests. Never inherited from the workspace root. A shipped module may not depend on a skipped one outside its test tables.

release.description: [release]: how a release is named and who publishes it (docs/user/release.md). The workspace root's table governs the whole workspace.

tag.description: The git tag of a release; {version} stands for the released version. Default "v{version}".

publish.description: Who publishes a release: "ci" (the pushed tag starts CI), "local" (jk release runs jk publish on the tag) or "none". Default: inferred from the destination and the CI files. `jk release --publish` overrides it for one run.

platforms.description: The platforms whose runtime images and native executables a release must carry; `jk publish --stage` uploads each from its own platform. Default: the host's platform alone.

files.description: Files besides jk.toml that carry the declared version. `jk release` rewrites the pattern's one group in each to the next version, in the commit that starts it.

pattern.description: A regular expression with exactly one group: the version.

export-dependencies.description: [export-dependencies]: one dependency per key — a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact[:version] string (versionless = platform-managed), "managed" on a catalog short name a platform BOM covers, or { group, name, version, features, ... }. A bare version is an exact pin; ^ ~ ranges and latest are opt-in.

dependencies.description: [dependencies]: one dependency per key — a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact[:version] string (versionless = platform-managed), "managed" on a catalog short name a platform BOM covers, or { group, name, version, features, ... }. A bare version is an exact pin; ^ ~ ranges and latest are opt-in.

provided-dependencies.description: [provided-dependencies]: one dependency per key — a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact[:version] string (versionless = platform-managed), "managed" on a catalog short name a platform BOM covers, or { group, name, version, features, ... }. A bare version is an exact pin; ^ ~ ranges and latest are opt-in.

runtime-dependencies.description: [runtime-dependencies]: one dependency per key — a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact[:version] string (versionless = platform-managed), "managed" on a catalog short name a platform BOM covers, or { group, name, version, features, ... }. A bare version is an exact pin; ^ ~ ranges and latest are opt-in.

test-dependencies.description: [test-dependencies]: one dependency per key — a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact[:version] string (versionless = platform-managed), "managed" on a catalog short name a platform BOM covers, or { group, name, version, features, ... }. A bare version is an exact pin; ^ ~ ranges and latest are opt-in.

plugin-dependencies.description: [plugin-dependencies]: refused — jk lock writes a pinned third-party plugin's SDK floor (jk-plugin-sdk, jk-host) into jk-lock.toml under the plugin scope itself; declare the plugin under [plugins].

processor-dependencies.description: [processor-dependencies]: one dependency per key — a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact[:version] string (versionless = platform-managed), "managed" on a catalog short name a platform BOM covers, or { group, name, version, features, ... }. A bare version is an exact pin; ^ ~ ranges and latest are opt-in.

test-processor-dependencies.description: [test-processor-dependencies]: one dependency per key — a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact[:version] string (versionless = platform-managed), "managed" on a catalog short name a platform BOM covers, or { group, name, version, features, ... }. A bare version is an exact pin; ^ ~ ranges and latest are opt-in. The reserved key inherit (default true) says whether compile-test also runs [processor-dependencies]; inherit = false makes this table compile-test's whole processor path.

inherit.description: true: compile-test runs [processor-dependencies] plus this table. false: this table alone, as Maven's testCompile runs only its own annotationProcessorPaths; with no entries, compile-test discovers processors on its classpath.

platform-dependencies.description: [platform-dependencies]: one dependency per key — a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact[:version] string (versionless = platform-managed), "managed" on a catalog short name a platform BOM covers, or { group, name, version, features, ... }. A bare version is an exact pin; ^ ~ ranges and latest are opt-in.

managed-dependencies.description: [managed-dependencies]: one managed version per key — a group:artifact:version string, a catalog short name with a version, or { group, name, version }. The entry pins the version a transitive dependency on the module resolves to, as Maven's inline dependencyManagement does; a version is required and the entry is not a classpath dependency of its own.

dev-dependencies.description: [dev-dependencies]: one dependency per key — a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact[:version] string (versionless = platform-managed), "managed" on a catalog short name a platform BOM covers, or { group, name, version, features, ... }. A bare version is an exact pin; ^ ~ ranges and latest are opt-in.

test-dev-dependencies.description: [test-dev-dependencies]: one dependency per key — a version string when the key is a catalog short name, a group:artifact[:version] string (versionless = platform-managed), "managed" on a catalog short name a platform BOM covers, or { group, name, version, features, ... }. A bare version is an exact pin; ^ ~ ranges and latest are opt-in.

node.description: The Node.js toolchain and node build (docs/user/node.md). At the top: node = 24 (a floor), "24.21.0" (a suggestion), "=24.21.0" (exact) or "lts". As a table: [node] with version and the build settings; every setting is inferred from package.json and the lockfile when unset.

version.description: The node version, as for node = … at the top.

workspace.description: Inherit the version from the workspace root.

package-manager.description: The package manager that installs and runs scripts. By default the lockfile decides, then packageManager or devEngines in package.json, else npm. Yarn means Yarn Berry; Yarn 1 is refused.

framework.description: The framework, which sets the output directory, dev port, inlined variable prefixes and server start. By default jk reads it from the scripts and config files.

install.description: The command that installs dependencies, in place of jk's frozen install (npm ci, pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, …).

build.description: What jk build runs: a package.json script name, or { npx = "…" } / { exec = "…" }.

test.description: The package.json script node-test runs; by default the test script, when there is one.

dev.description: The package.json script jk dev runs as the dev server; by default dev.

start.description: The command that runs a server output, which makes the module runnable by jk run and imageable by jk image. Inferred for Next standalone, Nuxt, SvelteKit with adapter-node and similar.

out.description: The directory the build writes, relative to the node directory; the framework's by default (dist for Vite).

classpath-root.description: The directory inside the jar the output is packaged under; static by default when a JVM module depends on this one, so Spring Boot serves it.

webapp-root.description: The path inside the war the output is placed at, for a [war] module that consumes it; the war's root by default.

env-prefixes.description: Prefixes of the environment variables the framework inlines into the bundle, whose values are part of the build's cache key; the framework's by default (VITE_, NEXT_PUBLIC_, …).

dev-port.description: The port the dev server listens on, which jk dev waits for before printing the ready line.

dir.description: The directory holding package.json: the module itself, src/main/node in a JVM module, or a project directory above the module (a front end at the workspace root that this module builds).

inputs.description: What the build and tests read, relative to the node build's directory (files, directories, globs). Unset, they read the whole directory; set it when that directory is a workspace root.

skip.description: When true, no node step of the module runs and packaging uses the output already built; --skip-node and JK_SKIP_NODE do the same for one run.

steps.description: [[node.steps]]: extra cached steps that run a package.json script (run), a package binary from node_modules (npx) or a program (exec), placed before the build, the tests or packaging.

name.description: The step's name; its task is node-step-<name>.

run.description: A package.json script to run with the module's package manager.

npx.description: A package binary and its arguments, resolved from node_modules only unless allow-unlocked is set.

exec.description: A program and its arguments, run with the locked Node.js first on PATH.

before.description: The step this one runs ahead of; build by default.

tier.description: test runs the step with the test tier, so --skip-tests leaves it out and [test] failures applies.

inputs.description: Module-relative files, directories or globs the step reads (../ allowed). With inputs the step is keyed on them alone; without, on the whole node tree.

outputs.description: Paths relative to the node directory the step writes, cached and restored. A step with none is a check, cached as passed.

allow-unlocked.description: An npx of a package the install does not hold is fetched (at its @version, else the registry's latest, which enters the key) instead of refused.

exports.description: Named outputs a sibling module may consume, as name = path; each path must be the output directory or a step's output.

inherit.description: Cargo-style inheritance from the workspace root.

dependency.description: A dependency's inline table. Its source is one of version (a Maven coordinate, with group and name or the catalog short name the key spells), git, path, sha256 (with version, a pinned jar) or workspace = true; git and path read the coordinate from that project, and group alone leaves the version to a platform BOM.

group.description: Maven group; absent, the catalog short name's.

name.description: Maven artifact, or the workspace member, when the key is another handle; absent, the key.

version.description: An exact pin, a ^ ~ range or latest.

git.description: A git repository to build the dependency from.

path.description: A local jk, Maven or Gradle project to build; beside git, the sub-directory of the repository.

sha256.description: With version and group, the jar pinned to the bytes of this sha256.

workspace.description: A workspace member, or a version the workspace's [workspace.dependencies] shares.

optional.description: Left out of the default resolution; a [features] entry pulls it in by name.

kind.description: tests: a workspace sibling's test classes or a Maven test-jar, in a test scope only.

classifier.description: The classified jar of a Maven coordinate.

fixtures.description: A workspace sibling's fixtures output, in a test scope only.

exclude.description: group:artifact coordinates (either may be *) pruned from this dependency's subtree.

features.description: The dependency's features to turn on.

default-features.description: false: leave the dependency's default features off.

submodules.description: false: check the git repository out without its submodules.

verify-signed.description: true: refuse a git commit whose signature does not verify.

workspace-dependency.description: A [workspace.dependencies] entry's inline table: a version or a git source the members share.

group.description: Maven group; absent, the catalog short name's. Required beside git.

version.description: An exact pin, a ^ ~ range or latest.

git.description: A git repository to build the dependency from.

path.description: Beside git, the sub-directory of the repository.

exclude.description: group:artifact coordinates (either may be *) pruned from this dependency's subtree.

submodules.description: false: check the git repository out without its submodules.

verify-signed.description: true: refuse a git commit whose signature does not verify.
